prompt: A scale drawing uses a scale of $1$ centimeter to $250$ centimeters. A wall measures $6$ centimeters on the drawing. What is the actual length of the wall, in meters?
hint: There are two jobs in this question: scaling up from the drawing, and changing units. Do them one at a time.

hints.text: There are two jobs in this question: scaling up from the drawing, and changing units. Do them one at a time.
Each centimeter on the drawing stands for $250$ real centimeters, so the wall is $6 \times 250$ centimeters long. Then change centimeters to meters.
The wall is $1500$ centimeters, and $1500 \div 100 = 15$, so the actual length is $15$ meters.

learningObjective: Apply a scale factor and convert the result to the requested unit.
explanation: Each drawing centimeter represents $250$ actual centimeters, so $6$ cm represents $6 \times 250 = 1500$ cm.
The question asks for meters: $1500 \text{ cm} \div 100 = 15$ meters.
Skipping the conversion gives $1500$, which will be one of the answer choices.

alternativeExplanations.title: Two-step questions hide the second step
steps: The scale work and the unit conversion are separate tasks, and only the first one is obvious.
Underline the unit the question asks for — here, "in meters" — before computing anything.
On the SAT, a question that changes units mid-problem is doing so deliberately.
